scope: Same-address PrefixRead P-N-P discriminator for KMBUS_EEPROM_READ 0x43 on local WB2A / VDensHO1 / 20C2.
conclusions: At 0x0001/1 the presence of the exact six-byte PrefixRead materially changed the response in a controlled sub-second P-N-P sequence: 88 -> 87 -> 88. This is direct local evidence that the extra request bytes are not universally ignored.
At 0x000A/5 no PrefixRead effect was observed: all three results were 4000000000.
The higher-address blocks remain unsuitable for EEPROM interpretation: 0x0078 and 0x00A0 continued to return repeated two-byte words that changed during the P-N-P sequence.
The 0x0078 sequence changed from repeated 5497 to repeated d301 even though both prefixed requests were nominally identical, proving that this response class can change on sub-second timescales.

The 0x00A0 sequence returned repeated 5498, then repeated f201 without prefix, then repeated 5497 with prefix. Because the two prefixed controls disagree, the no-prefix difference cannot be attributed solely to PrefixRead.

The strongest justified statement is now: PrefixRead can affect at least one local 0x43 transaction, but its exact semantics (routing selector, mode selector, or another request parameter) are not yet proven.
next_step: Repeat only 0x0001/1 in isolated fresh P300 sessions with a balanced prefixed/no-prefix order so protocol-session carryover and sequence bias are removed.
Do not expand the 0x43 address map until the isolated 0x0001 effect is reproduced.
Deprioritize semantic decoding of repeated high-address words until their transaction/state mechanism is understood.
